presentation.body: Every coding agent on this machine writes its conversations somewhere different, in its own format, and nobody reopens those terminals. Transcript Lake follows Claude Code, Codex, OMP, Droid and Kimi as they write and keeps one local archive of every session, turn, tool call and token count.
presentation.title: Nothing you ever told an AI is lost again

presentation.body: Names, keys and paths are replaced on the way in, so the archive is safe to keep. Nothing leaves this machine: the Lake lives under LAKE_DATA (default ~/.transcript-lake), vendor transcript stores are only ever read, and daily NDJSON partitions are append-only.
presentation.title: Masked before anything is stored

presentation.body: One supervised process is the whole ingest: each source append is masked, appended to today's partition and projected to Oko before its byte cursor moves, so a restart resumes where it stopped. This step is satisfied once the Lake holds partitions of your own transcripts.
presentation.title: Follow your agents as they write

presentation.body: Plain SQL over the canonical DuckDB views - events, sessions, tools_daily, tokens_daily, hook_decisions - answers who solved this before, what a project cost in tokens, how long the work really took. The first rows returned are evidence no closed terminal could reconstruct.
presentation.command: transcript-lake query "SELECT runtime, count(*) AS events FROM events GROUP BY runtime"
presentation.title: Ask the archive a question
